newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Fla., plans $219 million refunding.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Fla., plans $219 million refunding.

text.p: Florida's Orange County will sell $219 million of tourism development tax revenue refunding bonds by competitive bid at 11 a.m. EDT on July 22, county officials said Friday.
The advance refunding issue will be insured by MBIA Insurance Corp and will have maturities out to 2021.
"It's a pretty straightforward structure," said Orange County Fiscal Administrator Lydia Brown.
Present value savings are estimated at a little over $9 million. The bonds are among the highest rated bed tax bonds in the
nation, A3 by Moody's Investors Service and single-A by Standard & Poor's Corp and Fitch Investors Service.
"In our 1994 refunding, we were the only tourist development tax credit with a single-A from both (rating agencies)," said Deputy Comptroller Jim Moye.

"We've been in the market with this particular credit since the early 1980s. The other factor is basically the strength of the tourism industry here in central Florida is really fantastic," Moye said.
The Orange County area is home to Walt Disney World and Universal Studios and claims the nation's second largest convention center.
